description: Verifies visible-grid finger taps stay under the finger, an existing pipe leg can be finger-tapped to start a tee branch, and the North arrow remains independently movable and rotatable.
steps: Open ISO, draw a clearly vertical pipe section upward and confirm its linked Section/leg direction reads Up rather than North; draw downward and confirm it reads Down. Then start a new run with one finger tap and immediately make a second finger tap on a different visible grid intersection; confirm that second tap creates the first pipe segment instead of being swallowed by the SVG grid, amber active-point marker, endpoint drag handler, or pipe hit area. Continue tapping several visible grid intersections, including near the left/top of the currently visible grid, and confirm every new pipe endpoint lands on an exact visible intersection and every normal snapped segment centerline overlays one visible grid line pixel-for-pixel for its entire length—vertical, up-right/down-left, or up-left/down-right—with no CSS-grid/rendering drift and no off-grid chord between intersections; then hold and drag the last amber endpoint to change its length/angle and release it, confirming no extra point or pipe segment is created and that same moved endpoint remains the amber active point; tap the next empty grid point and confirm the new pipe segment continues from the corrected endpoint; refresh the app and confirm the saved normal ISO endpoints and pipe centerlines still sit on those exact same lattice intersections/grid lines, then repeat grid tapping after zooming and in ELEVATION

With PIPE LINE active, finish a run at a visible endpoint, then finger-tap the middle of an existing pipe leg to accidentally start a tee and immediately press UNDO. Confirm the tee disappears, the split pipe rejoins into the original single leg, the amber active point returns to the endpoint where the run had ended before the tee, and the next intentional tap continues from that restored endpoint instead of from the middle of the pipe. Then turn SNAP OFF, finger-tap anywhere along the body/hit zone of an existing pipe leg (not an endpoint handle or dimension label) and confirm the tee junction locks to the nearest valid exact grid intersection on that pipe and becomes the amber active point; confirm tapping an endpoint still edits/drags the endpoint and tapping a dimension still edits the measurement instead of creating a tee; tap a new grid point upward or diagonal and confirm the branch endpoint lands exactly on that grid point, the tee straight-through run stays on the original pipe, and the bullhead automatically turns to exactly follow the new branch angle. Drag the branch endpoint to another angle and confirm the bullhead follows it, then select the tee and use ±15° once and confirm it trims the automatic branch orientation without moving the tee run; switch ISO / PLAN / ELEVATION and confirm both run and branch orientation remain matched to their pipes

Rough in a diagonal offset direction, then tap RISE and enter 3' and tap RUN and enter 4'. Confirm the selected leg automatically becomes a calculated 36.9° offset with 5' travel, its endpoint is positioned from the exact rise/run math rather than snapped back to a normal grid intersection, and hatch marks appear under the diagonal with the run guide pointing in the offset travel direction. Change RUN to 3' and confirm the same leg recalculates to 45° automatically and is noticeably steeper/shallower than the normal 90-degree grid leg: it must sit exactly halfway between the selected 45-degree screen diagonal plan axis (N/E/S/W) and vertical UP/DOWN, rather than following either axis or landing on an ordinary grid intersection. Confirm a 5' calculated offset travel is drawn at the same visual length scale as a normal 5' pipe leg and does not become longer simply because RISE and RUN were entered. Confirm the RUN and RISE guides remain proportional to each other and the hatch marks fill the triangular plane between the guides and offset travel. Rough the same test leg toward a different in-between plane and reapply the values; confirm the offset follows that rough plane without displaying N/E/S/W or UP/DOWN direction text. Rise and run remain independently tappable for editing; switch views and refresh to confirm the calculated offset geometry and values persist

On a mobile viewport, select a pipe and then a fitting and confirm the measurement/rise/run and rotate controls use a slim single-row horizontal strip with the long hint hidden, leaving most of the drawing visible; scroll the strip sideways if needed to reach every control. Confirm MEASURE AUTO is the normal working mode: only the selected pipe shows its C-C/rise/run dimensions and offset guides, while other pipe measurements stay hidden. Cycle to MEASURE ALL and confirm every dimension can be reviewed, then cycle to MEASURE OFF and confirm all dimension callouts disappear while pipe, endpoints, notes, and drawing taps remain usable. Return to AUTO, refresh, and confirm the selected measurement mode persists

Tap CHOOSE EXISTING PHOTO and confirm the phone photo library/file picker opens without forcing the camera; select an existing photo and confirm it appears beneath the grid. Then tap TAKE PHOTO and confirm the camera capture flow remains available separately

Press NORTH ARROW and confirm the N arrow appears inside the currently visible drawing area without scrolling; draw a true vertical ISO pipe section and confirm its Section direction reads Up when drawn upward and Down when drawn downward, regardless of North-arrow rotation. Then draw or select a horizontal/diagonal plan-direction pipe section and note its Section direction; rotate the North arrow 15 degrees and 90 degrees and confirm only the plan compass direction updates automatically relative to the new job North while the vertical section remains Up/Down and all pipe endpoints stay fixed
Switch through ISO, PLAN, and ELEVATION again and confirm the same shared pipe geometry converts automatically while the North arrow keeps its saved position and rotation
expected: The first mobile finger tap sets a start point and the second finger tap reliably creates the first pipe segment, including when the first point is the amber active endpoint marker; finger taps remain exactly aligned to visible intersections and every normal snapped ISO pipe segment follows the exact same rendered grid geometry 100% from endpoint to endpoint, with its centerline directly covering the visible grid line rather than merely connecting approximate intersections, holding and dragging the last endpoint changes only that endpoint and does not create an extra point or segment on release; that same moved endpoint stays active so the next intentional tap continues the run from the corrected point. Touching the middle of an existing pipe leg creates a tee junction locked to an exact valid grid intersection and makes it the active branch start, even when general SNAP is off; the next tap draws the branch exactly to the tapped grid point. If that tee was accidental and UNDO is pressed before drawing the branch, the tee split is fully reversed, the original pipe leg is restored, and the active amber point returns to the endpoint that was active before the tee so drawing can continue without redoing the run. The tee straight-through run stays aligned with the original pipe while the bullhead automatically follows the branch segment angle, including after branch endpoint edits and ISO/Plan/Elevation conversion; manual rotation remains an optional trim. Entering RISE and RUN automatically converts the selected diagonal leg into a calculated offset: the app computes travel with the rise/run triangle, computes the offset angle, positions the ISO diagonal from that math instead of normal grid-axis snapping, and shows hatch marks under the diagonal to identify offset travel direction. A 3'-rise by 4'-run offset shows 5' travel and about 36.9°. Equal rise and run recalculate to 45° and the offset is the exact visual bisector between the normal diagonal plan grid axis (N/E/S/W) and UP or DOWN, so it is clearly on a different plane from an ordinary 90-degree run. The calculated travel uses the same visual measurement scale as ordinary pipe, so equal measured travels appear equal in drawn length; the RUN/RISE guides remain proportionate and the offset UI does not add compass-direction labels. Tapping either button opens measurement entry and each value remains independently editable. On mobile, the selected-pipe/fitting editor stays as a slim horizontally scrollable strip instead of a large box covering the drawing. MEASURE AUTO keeps the drawing clear by showing dimensions only for the selected pipe; MEASURE ALL shows the full dimension set for review and MEASURE OFF hides callouts entirely without changing pipe geometry. Compact labels remain editable and the chosen mode persists. Existing photos can be selected from the phone library without forcing camera capture, while TAKE PHOTO remains available separately. One shared drawing drives all three views, and the North arrow appears on-screen and can be dragged and rotated independently. True vertical ISO sections always report Up/Down; rotating job North changes only plan compass labels and never relabels a riser as North/South.

name: Use tabbed Takeoffs and preserve manufacturer-specific data
covers: Aquatherm socket fusion insertion and timing
NUPI NIRON socket fusion insertion and timing
HDPE butt fusion wall bead heat and cooling reference
HDPE socket fusion depth heat and cooling reference
description: Verifies the tabbed Takeoffs screen still keeps manufacturer/product dimensions attached to the selected fitting.
steps: Open TAKEOFFS and use the GROOVED tab
Select Victaulic No. 100-5D 90 degree Long Radius Elbow at 4 inches and confirm the result, then switch to Gruvlok Fig. 7050-5D at 4 inches
Select Gruvlok Fig. 7072 Concentric Reducer at 8 x 6

Open FUSION PIPE. In Aquatherm Socket select 2 inch above 40°F and confirm 1-1/16 inch insertion, 24 sec heat, 8 sec transition and 6 min cool. Tap START HEAT and confirm the timer bar immediately shows Aquatherm heat with a large dark 0:24 countdown on a high-contrast light background plus a readable STOP TIMER button; tap STOP TIMER and confirm it changes to STOPPED with remaining time, then tap START HEAT again and confirm the countdown restarts. In NUPI / NIRON Socket select 2 inch SDR 17 and confirm 1-1/16 inch insertion, 10 sec heat, 8 sec max changeover, 30 sec clamped and 6 min total cool. In HDPE Socket select 2 IPS PE4710 and confirm 0.875 inch depth, 24–28 sec heat and 60 sec initial cool. In HDPE Butt enter 8.625 inch OD and DR 11 and confirm about 0.784 inch wall, bead-controlled heat and about 8.6 min minimum cooling under fusion pressure
expected: Only the selected Takeoffs category is shown, both 4 inch 5D long-radius elbows show 24 inches center-to-end, the Gruvlok 8 x 6 reducer shows 5 inches end-to-end, and each result names its brand/product source. The Fusion Pipe tab shows manufacturer-specific socket insertion/timing references, PP butt timing references, HDPE bead/wall/cooling calculations, and clear qualified-procedure warnings rather than inventing unsupported fitting dimensions. Fusion timer START controls immediately launch a high-contrast, easily readable labeled countdown, STOP TIMER reliably halts it and shows the remaining time, and START can restart it.

covers: no repeated app title/status/toolbox header on tab pages
calculator opens with no app title, status, toolbox revision, or Calculator heading above its screen

seven common fraction quick keys including 3/8 and 5/8
standard and extra heavy wrench size
description: Verifies the main calculator fits a phone screen cleanly and the Elbow / Offset tools switch inside a fixed layout with a useful visual for each calculator.
steps: On a 375px mobile viewport open CALC and confirm there is no app title, Ready status, FIELD TOOLBOX revision, or Calculator heading above the calculator screen; confirm the calculator display, four-column number pad, unit controls, and all seven fraction buttons 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4, and 7/8 fit in one row within the screen width with usable touch targets and no horizontal scrolling
Open several other bottom tabs and confirm none show the repeated Pipefitter Field Pro / FIELD TOOLBOX / Ready header at the top

Open TOOLS, switch to ELBOW / OFFSET, and tap CUT DOWN 90, EQUAL SPREAD, SPECIAL TWO 90s, and ANY-ANGLE OFFSET; confirm the tab row stays the same size, only the selected calculator changes, and every calculator shows its own pipe/elbow picture

In SPECIAL TWO 90s enter 11 inches with 4 inch NPS LR 90 elbows and confirm each elbow is cut to about 85.220 degrees; then open REF WRENCH SIZES and confirm separate Standard and Extra heavy columns remain
expected: Bottom tabs open directly into their useful content without the repeated Pipefitter Field Pro / Ready / FIELD TOOLBOX header, while CALC starts directly at the calculator with no title/status/toolbox/Calculator writing above its screen. The calculator stays within the phone screen with thumb-friendly controls and all seven common fraction keys, including 3/8 and 5/8, fit in one row without horizontal scrolling; the four Elbow / Offset tabs switch without reformatting the page and each has a clear visual, and the existing formulas and wrench references keep their prior results.

Select Intersection at Any Degree, enter 45 degrees, build marks, and confirm the FORMULA + MARKS tab opens with the complement miter reference and 16-line sequence 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1

name: Search the offline pipefitter field reference
covers: pipe weight per foot by NPS and schedule
pipe plus contents support load calculator
plain-English contents specific gravity explanation and presets
single and double strut manufacturer-capacity check
insulation and concentrated valve load adder
concrete anchor tension shear interaction screen
thermal movement cold insulation and riser guidance
description: Verifies a pipefitter can search useful trade topics without leaving the app and jump into the matching built-in tool.
steps: Open SEARCH and confirm duplicate calculator/reference topics such as offsets, fitting takeoffs, fusion and pipe OD are not listed there

Search Rigging, tap the Rigging header, and confirm a detailed guide opens. Enter 2000 lb, 2 carrying legs, 60 degrees from horizontal and factor 1.0; confirm idealized leg tension is about 1155 lb and the screen explicitly says this is not allowable capacity and must be checked against rated gear/lift plan

Go back, search Hydrostatic and pneumatic testing, open it, enter 100 ft water head, SG 1 and 0 psi at the high point; confirm about 43.30 psi static head. Confirm the page does not invent the required test pressure and includes pneumatic stored-energy cautions

Open Supports and confirm the threaded-rod table shows 3/8 in = 730 lb, 1/2 in = 1,350 lb, 5/8 in = 2,160 lb and 3/4 in = 3,230 lb; select 4 in Schedule 40 and confirm bare pipe is about 10.79 lb/ft, enter a 10 ft supported length with Water — SG 1.00 and confirm the page explains that specific gravity is liquid density/weight relative to water, that SG 0.80 weighs about 80% of the same volume of water and SG 1.20 about 120%, and confirm the page calculates pipe plus contents and screens a rod size while warning to add insulation/fittings/valves; confirm strut and concrete-anchor sections require the exact published manufacturer value instead of inventing universal single/double-strut or anchor capacities; use the 48 in trapeze example with 500,500 lb at 12,36 in and confirm left and right reactions are each about 500 lb; confirm insulation/valve load addition, cantilever moment, beam-clamp utilization and anchor tension/shear screens work and that the page warns about rod compression/buckling, concentrated loads, cold insulation, risers and thermal movement; then open Welding and Material Identification results and confirm each opens a useful detailed field guide
expected: SEARCH opens substantial complementary field-reference pages instead of one-line summaries. Rigging includes an idealized sling-angle/load-share planning calculator with strong WLL/lift-plan guardrails; testing includes static-head math without inventing a required test pressure; welding, safety, supports and materials provide actionable field checklists. Supports includes MSS threaded-rod tension values, pipe weight/load math and rod screening, trapeze reaction math for multiple pipes, added insulation and concentrated loads, cantilever and beam-clamp checks, anchor tension/shear interaction screening, and detailed spacing/thermal/cold/riser/buckling guidance, while product-specific checks require verified published capacities rather than unsafe generic ratings.

full manual pages tables diagrams and index available in-app
tubing bend layout from finished points

Pipe Fitters Blue Book field math companion

description: Verifies the dedicated Tubing tab gives usable centerline geometry, SAG full-layout marking, rotation guidance and real-world visual references without assuming a universal bender mark convention.
steps: Open MANUAL and confirm the actual uploaded Audel PDF is displayed in the tab with full pages available to scroll and an OPEN FULL MANUAL control; tap several compact topic controls and confirm each opens the uploaded manual at that topic's corresponding section/page instead of page 1; confirm the topic strip names major manual subjects without replacing the PDF content

Open TUBING on mobile and confirm the LAYOUT guide starts with a clear 90 degree diagram labeling DATUM END, theoretical corner C, T1/T2 tangent points, CLR, setback and finished legs. Enter CLR 3 in and bend angle 90 degrees; confirm bend allowance is about 4.712 in and tangent setback is 3.000 in, and confirm the guide says to transfer geometry to the actual bender start/arrow convention and re-measure later finished points from one datum

Open OFFSET, enter 6 in at 30 degrees and confirm centerline travel is 12.000 in and straight advance/run is about 10.392 in; confirm the multi-bend guide says to number bends, record angle/rotation, and return to the same datum rather than chaining errors
Open ROTATION, enter side 4 in and vertical 3 in and confirm true offset is 5.000 in and rotation is about 36.9 degrees, with a warning to define the viewing/datum end

Open SAG METHOD and confirm SAG is explicitly defined as Setback, Advance and Gain. Enter radius 2.5 in and 90 degrees; confirm setback 2.500 in, advance about 3.927 in and gain about 1.073 in. Confirm the worked example places S at 17.500 in and A at 21.427 in when C is 20.000 in, and the guide explains datum, S/C/A marks, bend numbering, rotation, reverse/left/right handling and springback

Open BEND DESIGN and confirm compression, draw and roll/push bending are explained; confirm the Lister guide rules show 2 x D as the standard draw-bend radius rule of thumb and 7 x D as the conservative roll-bending minimum guideline, plus multi-radius/tooling and difficult-geometry warnings. Expand common tube sizes and confirm both metric and imperial examples are present. Open FIELD MATH and confirm the Blue Book companion identifies common piping angles, rolling offsets, pipe bends and trig as source topics; confirm 30 degree offset travel multiplier 2.000, 45 degree multiplier 1.414, rolling true-offset geometry, setback, arc/advance and gain formulas are shown. Open PHOTO REFS and confirm a real stainless bend photo is visible plus links to real hand-bender references; confirm there is no SWAG / SWAGE tubing subtab
expected: The MANUAL tab displays the actual uploaded Audel PDF rather than a shortened rewrite, keeps a compact topic guide whose controls deep-link to their corresponding sections/pages in the uploaded manual, keeps the current-document warning, and provides a full-manual open control. The Tubing tab opens with an understandable labeled bend picture, provides correct centerline bend, offset, rolled-offset and SAG math, adds Lister Tube design/manufacturability guidance and a Blue Book-style field-math companion without copying book pages, and keeps real-world photo references to connect geometry to actual bent tubing and bender tooling.

name: Do not guess an unsupported fitting takeoff
description: Verifies drawing, tab, and reference changes do not weaken the fitting-dimension guardrail.
steps: Open TAKEOFFS and choose the SOCKET-WELD tab
Select a Union and a size/class without a common loaded value
Press CHECK SOCKET TAKEOFF and then ENTER ACTUAL TAKEOFF
expected: The app says the actual fitting takeoff is required and sends the user to the custom takeoff form instead of inventing a number.
